skill.name: service-mesh-expert
skill.description: Guides Istio and Linkerd architecture, traffic management, mTLS, observability, resilience, progressive delivery, and multi-cluster service mesh design.
skill.summary: Design and troubleshoot secure, observable service meshes for Kubernetes workloads.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a resource path. The skill contains guidance only and shows no command execution or malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 23 uses Markdown backticks to format a documentation path. It contains no Ruby code, shell command, execution directive, or user-controlled command input.

content.value_statement: Service mesh choices can create routing, security, and operational complexity. This skill provides structured guidance for Istio and Linkerd architecture, policies, observability, and resilience.
actual_capabilities: Assesses requirements and proposes Istio or Linkerd mesh topologies.
Explains routing, load balancing, retries, circuit breakers, and traffic splitting.
Designs mTLS, authorization, namespace isolation, and certificate management approaches.
Plans metrics, tracing, logging, and resource monitoring for mesh operations.
Guides multi-cluster discovery, federation, failover, and progressive delivery.
Produces validation steps and operational runbook outlines.
limitations: It provides guidance and does not inspect or modify a live cluster.
Recommendations require validation against installed versions, providers, and organizational policies.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the published file structure.
It does not replace production testing or review by authorized platform and security teams.

use_cases.title: Plan a Kubernetes Mesh
use_cases.description: Compare requirements and create a phased topology, security, observability, and rollout plan.

use_cases.title: Secure Service Communication
use_cases.description: Define mTLS adoption and authorization boundaries for services and namespaces.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Mesh Reliability
use_cases.description: Structure investigation steps for routing failures, retry storms, latency, and cross-cluster connectivity.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Mesh Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how a service mesh would help this Kubernetes application: [application details]. Cover benefits, costs, and required components.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn whether a service mesh fits a simple Kubernetes environment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an mTLS Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased mTLS rollout for [cluster details]. Include prerequisites, permissive mode, policy isolation, validation, rollback, and strict enforcement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Introduce encrypted service communication with controlled risk.

prompt_templates.title: Design Canary Traffic
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Istio or Linkerd traffic splitting for [service]. Include weights, health signals, failure thresholds, observability, promotion, and rollback steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a measurable canary deployment process.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a Multi-Cluster Mesh
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-cluster mesh for [requirements]. Address trust boundaries, discovery, failover, traffic policy, certificates, telemetry, capacity, testing, and operations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an advanced architecture for resilient cross-cluster communication.

output_examples.input: Plan strict mTLS for three namespaces with minimal disruption.
output: Confirm proxy coverage and certificate health in each namespace.
Enable permissive mTLS and monitor plaintext traffic.
Apply namespace authorization policies with explicit service identities.
Move one namespace at a time to strict mode.
Validate connectivity, telemetry, and rollback after each change.

output_examples.input: Outline a canary release for the checkout service.
output_examples.output: Begin with a small traffic share, track latency and error budgets, stop on threshold breaches, then increase traffic through defined stages.
Check endpoint discovery, gateway reachability, certificate trust, routing policy, and telemetry correlation. Test each network path before changing retry behavior.

best_practices: Provide cluster topology, mesh version, traffic goals, trust boundaries, and failure symptoms.
Request staged changes with measurable validation and rollback criteria.
Test routing, security, and failover behavior in a representative environment before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not enforce strict mTLS before confirming proxy coverage and plaintext dependencies.
Do not add retries without budgets, timeouts, and protection against retry amplification.
Do not accept generic configuration advice without checking versions, providers, and existing policies.

faq.question: Does this skill install Istio or Linkerd?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation planning, configuration guidance, validation steps, and troubleshooting approaches.

faq.question: Which service meshes does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Istio and Linkerd while applying general cloud-native networking and service mesh principles.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready policies?
faq.answer: It can propose policy designs, but authorized teams must review and test them against the target environment.

faq.question: Does it support multi-cluster environments?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers federation, service discovery, trust, failover, telemetry, and traffic management across clusters.

faq.question: What information improves troubleshooting?
faq.answer: Provide mesh versions, topology, affected services, recent changes, policy details, proxy status, logs, metrics, and traces.

faq.question: Can it help with progressive delivery?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan canary or blue-green traffic shifts with health signals, thresholds, promotion stages, and rollback criteria.
